opening_message:
Ticket 1: Andrew Mann (employee ID E014) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E014.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee E014 (Andrew Mann) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write (admin only for owners; write is within policy). Grant write access.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E014 (Andrew Mann) is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max; recommend read. Note: this conflicts with HR note claiming full-time employee.
reason: Employee E014 (Andrew Mann) requests write access to Payroll. The HR note claims full-time Payroll Specialist, which would permit write. However, the Security note (from the Security database) indicates the employee is a contractor with only basic security training, for whom write exceeds the allowed maximum (contractors max out at read without advanced training). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive, policy-compliant interpretation: grant the maximum allowed level for a contractor with basic training, which is read. Grant read.

Let me submit decision: read, with reasoning that security database indicates contractor with basic training, making write exceed the max, and conflicting HR note; grant max of read.
